summary: newOfflineHistoryCmd (internal/cli/offline.go) omits the "caveats" key entirely from its response map when caveatIfEmpty returns nil, instead of embedding the nil directly in the map literal (which JSON-marshals to "caveats": null). printOffline's own caveats-survives-select reattachment (see offline-caveats-survive-select.json) is hardened as defense-in-depth to match: it now checks whether the captured caveats value actually marshals to something other than the JSON literal "null" before re-attaching it after --select filtering, since "present in the map" and "has a real value" are different things for a typed-nil Go slice boxed in an `any` (c != nil is always true there -- the check has to happen on the marshaled bytes, not the interface value). Together these mean "caveats" key present == real caveat content, always, across every offline command -- a caller can test for the key's presence instead of having to null-check its value too. Any future offline command that builds its own caveats value must avoid embedding a possibly-nil slice directly in a map literal it always includes, or rely on printOffline's hardened reattachment to strip it, not both being silently correct only by accident.
reason: Round-11 verification NEW 3: offline_history --select ... returned {"caveats": null, "items": [...]} when there were no caveats to report, instead of omitting the key. The report noted this as a regression risk from the round-8 "caveats always survives --select" fix (offline-caveats-survive-select.json), which appears to have made the key unconditional rather than present-only -- a caller can't test for presence and has to null-check the value too.
validated_outcome: go build/vet/test/govulncheck and verify_skill.py all green. Existing offline_test.go coverage continues to pass; offline_history's own map literal no longer includes a nil-valued "caveats" key when facts are non-empty, verified by inspection of the JSON encoding path (a nil []string boxed in an any marshals to the literal null, which is exactly what disappeared from the response).
